body:
The mechanism is exactly what your title suggests, and it's fully traceable in jax's own Python source. `_set_up_aliases` in `jax/_src/interpreters/mlir.py` (~line 1490) builds implicit donation aliases with a plain FIFO queue keyed only on `(aval, memory_kind)`, shape, dtype, and memory kind, with zero awareness of which output actually derives from which input. It walks the flattened output leaves in pytree order and greedily hands each one the next available donated input of matching shape. That's precisely why reordering `(ys, state)` to `(state, ys)` changes the outcome: it changes which leaf gets matched first in the FIFO queue, and why you need 3+ same-shaped leaves to see it.

What I can't trace from this repo is the second half: why a mismatched alias hint actually produces corrupted values on GPU instead of just silently-safe extra buffer reuse. That's XLA's buffer-assignment and copy-insertion machinery, which lives in openxla/xla as a compiled dependency, not in jax-ml/jax's Python source, so I can't confirm the GPU-vs-CPU asymmetry beyond noting the aliasing hint itself is identical on both backends and CPU apparently tolerates it safely while GPU doesn't.

For what it's worth, this isn't a first occurrence: #20088 (closed) reported a similar donation-plus-something producing garbage values, different trigger (sharding constraint, CPU) but the same underlying shape-based-aliasing-without-dataflow-awareness category. Given the fix here means making `_set_up_aliases` dataflow-aware rather than shape-aware, a real change to core donation semantics, that feels like something for the jax team to scope rather than something to hand a PR for unprompted.
